messages:
maya: Heads up — intermittent nondeterminism in eval runner v2.3.1 when running quantized models. Repro steps below.

maya: On CI (linux, docker) same seed, same prompt, 10 runs -> outputs differ in 3/10. Locally (mac) they're stable.

aj: :thinking: which sampler + scheduler?

maya: We're using the interleaver sampler with top_p=0.92 temp=0.7. worker_pool=4, batch_size=8. seed pinned at 42.

maya: Config dump:
```
model: redwood-7b-q8
runner: v2.3.1
sampler:
  type: interleaver
  top_p: 0.92
  temperature: 0.7
seed: 42
worker_pool: 4
```

zheng: Can you paste the minimal script + stdout diff? Also CI artifacts link?

maya: gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcdef12345 — has the script and two outputs that diverge at token 27.

sam: I hit this earlier — might be RNG state shared across workers after quant kernels call into thread-local PRNG in the C++ runtime. Could be seeding per worker not per sample.

eva: Do we see any tokenization differences? sometimes tokenizer padding/offsets cause early divergence.

maya: I checked tokenization hashes, they match. Diff shows same tokens until a sampling decision then different branch of top-p.

ci-bot: Build 2026-03-19T12:34:56Z: runner-v2.3.1 deployed to canary

aj: Try running with worker_pool=1 and with `--deterministic-scheduler` flag.

maya: Ran with worker_pool=1 — 10/10 identical. With deterministic-scheduler flag also stable.

zheng: So it's likely a concurrency-ordering issue in the interleaver sampler. Maybe RNG handoff not synchronized with batching order.

sam: Quick test: add per-sample PRNG state that includes (global_seed, sample_index, step) to derive rng. That would be invariant to ordering.

eva: Can you try a patch that seeds per-sample deterministically? quick sketch:
```
uint64_t derive_seed(uint64_t global, int sample_idx) {
  return splitmix64(global + 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL + sample_idx);
}
```

maya: I ran a local patch like that — stable across workers. CI still shows occasional divergence though (2/20).

aj: Hmm. Is there any asynchronous KV cache fetch or prefix cache that mutates order of requests? That can change timing and interleaving.

maya: There is a prefix cache async miss handler that will fetch from disk and then resume. Could change ordering.

zheng: If cache callback uses a different thread and doesn't account for sample_idx when merging RNG state, that explains it.

sam: Proposed fix: make RNG derivation purely deterministic from sample_idx+step; never touch global PRNG after startup. PRNG state per worker only used to generate unique offsets e.g., for dropout but not sampling decisions.

eva: Also add CI test: run 100 seeds across 4 workers and assert exact byte-eq outputs using the per-sample seeding. Should catch regressions.

maya: I'll open a PR with the per-sample seed change + CI test and link here.

maya: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/infra/pull/7123

ci-bot: PR 7123 created by maya. Labels: eng-ml, flaky-eval, high-priority :bug:

aj: Nice. If CI still flakes after that we need to trace kernel-level thread-local uses of rng libs like xoshiro or std::mt19937.

maya: Thanks all — filing an issue to audit native kernels for hidden RNG uses.

maya: TL;DR: Root cause likely ordering-sensitive RNG handoff across async cache / interleaver. Short-term: per-sample deterministic seeding. Long-term: audit kernels and make sampling decisions only depend on per-sample deterministic state. :thumbsup:
